bullets.title: Core PCE next week is the macro hinge: benign <0.3% favors risk-on, hot >0.3% pressures cyclicals
bullets.body: Multiple sources (22V, MS, OPCO) converge: if next week's CPI/PPI imply core PCE near 0.21–0.3%, it reinforces a higher neutral rate thesis and favors Growth/Value/AI stock-picking alpha. A hot print (>0.3%) biases yields higher, pressures cyclicals and momentum/AI theme baskets, and raises odds of Fed hikes later this year. MS notes AI theme rolling beta to 10yr yields is significantly above long-term medians, making the AI basket unusually rate-sensitive.

bullets.title: Fed shifting toward rate hikes; 22V sees 2yr yield toward 5%, gold less attractive
bullets.body: 22V Research's macro backdrop assessment: consumer spending, labor markets, and earnings point to accelerating demand, with the Fed bias shifting toward additional rate hikes later this year or early next year. 2-year yield likely headed toward 5%; gold attractiveness diminished by higher bond yields. Iran escalation risk could further fuel a hawkish Fed narrative and push Treasury yields higher.

bullets.title: S&P at 7,558; VIX 15.45; vol-control funds set to buy $12–15B as 1-month vol fades
bullets.body: S&P 500 up ~0.2% to 7,557.80, with futures reversing early losses to turn positive. VIX rose 2.5% to 15.45. OPCO and Hedgeye both flag vol-control funds requiring ~$12–15B in net buying as 1-month vol declines through mid-July; COR1M correlation at 3.95 (extremely low), with SPX 7500 seen as strong support with positive gamma across strikes.

bullets.title: Iran tensions minimal market impact; oil at $76/bbl; Hormuz bypass routes rebounding
bullets.body: Despite resumed U.S. strikes on Iran and Iran's infrastructure retaliation warnings, Brent crude fell to ~$76/bbl with oil barely moving—market dismissing escalation risk. Qatar is mediating US-Iran talks per NYT. UBS data shows Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic declining further while bypass route loadings at Yanbu rebound; UK maritime authority warns routes outside southern Hormuz are unprotected.

bullets.title: META surges 4% on SemiAnalysis AI compute report; $250B 2027 capex plan disclosed
bullets.body: META rallied ~4% after SemiAnalysis published a detailed positive report on the company's AI compute ramp, with Zuckerberg confirming $250B capex in 2027 (vs. prior $175–225B estimates) targeting 14GW compute by end-2027. Meta's custom ASIC from AVGO enters full production 2H26; compute expansion costs tracking well below analyst expectations, easing capex concerns. Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 model matches or exceeds Anthropic/OpenAI at 25% lower pricing.

bullets.title: HBM prices expected to double in 2027; hyperscaler datacenter capex revised up to +80% YoY
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Harlan Sur raises top-4 hyperscaler datacenter capex to +80% YoY in 2026E (from 70%+), with AI accelerator units rising to 16.3M in 2026 (+62%) and 23.3M in 2027 (+43%). HBM TAM modeled at $65B in 2026 (+94% YoY) and $129B in 2027 (+99%); HBM prices expected to double in 2027 with HBM4 estimated at $4–5/GB vs. ~$2 in H2 2026. Structural supply/demand tightness in memory expected to extend through CY28.

bullets.title: Micron commits $250B to US manufacturing through 2035; NY DRAM megafab underway
bullets.body: Micron announced a $250B investment commitment through 2035 to build multiple Terafabs in the US, with New York DRAM megafab construction already started. The announcement underscores the domestic semiconductor buildout narrative but the stock was trading down ~2.6% pre-market amid broader semis weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO cites accelerating growth toward $100B quarterly revenue; GPU rental rates up 5–10%
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang told MS analysts AI growth is broadening across labs, hyperscalers, and sovereigns, with three demand vectors: AI labs (20%), hyperscalers (50%), and AI clouds/enterprise (50%, highest growth). GPU rental rates are up 5–10% July YTD; H100 curve rising with provider price hikes. Rubin Ultra roadmap on track for next year with no slip to 2028.

bullets.title: AI theme rate sensitivity elevated; AI Services positively correlated to yields, AI Goods negatively
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Generative AI Baskets show rolling beta to 10yr yields significantly above long-term medians. AI Services companies are positively correlated to yields while AI Goods companies are negatively correlated—a split that matters heading into next week's inflation prints.

bullets.title: Euro area 2Q26 upside growth risks; JPM sees ECB hiking in September, BoE in November
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags Euro area 2Q26 GDP risks tilted to the upside: manufacturing output tracking 3% annualized gain, retail sales +0.8% annualized, car registrations +10%+ annualized. For 2H26, JPM calls for ECB rate hike in September (sticky core inflation at 2.4% YoY, persistent wage drift) and BoE hike in November. Le Pen's 15-month ban elapsed, clearing path for 2027 French presidential run; she polls above 30% in first round.

bullets.title: Dollar bull trend intact; EUR/USD biased toward 1.1065–1.1185; USD/JPY bullish above 160
bullets.body: JPMorgan FX technicals: DXY pullback is corrective with medium-term bull trend intact above 99.06–99.22 (200-day MA); setup favors push toward 102.72–103.05 with 105.08 measured move. EUR/USD negative bias below 1.15, targeting 1.1065–1.1185. USD/JPY bullish above 159.87–160.72 support after achieving 163.23 objective; next resistance 165.61. Contrarian view: JPY shorts are crowded at a time when Japan's economic conditions and policy backdrop are shifting positively.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler bond issuance ($132B YTD) creating supply fatigue; balance sheets more levered
bullets.body: JPMorgan warns hyperscalers have issued $132B senior unsecured bonds YTD plus ~$26B in project finance debt, with AI investment accelerating faster than transparency into capex needs. Hyperscaler balance sheets becoming progressively more levered, reducing scarcity value of paper. Amazon's $25B eight-tranche deal signaled limited visibility into future financing plans; tech spreads +3.6bp, media +6.6bp wider amid Middle East conflict.

bullets.title: China AI capex forecast raised 23% to $1T through 2030; 300K H200 chip imports expected in 2026
bullets.body: Jefferies raises China AI capex forecast 23% to $1T cumulative for 2026–2030, with China power demand for AI rising 31% to 34GW. China expected to import 300K H200 chips in 2026 and 100K in 2027; local AI chip output (Ascend 950) forecast to rise 18%. World AI Conference (WAIC) on July 17 to feature Premier Li Qiang with 1,100+ participating companies.

bullets.title: Top H1 tech performers almost all negative in Q3; narrow leadership beginning to rotate
bullets.body: Of the 20 top H1 performing stocks—nearly all in tech—only 2 are up in Q3, with the average return of top H1 performers now negative. Separately, Financials and Health Care sectors both flashed golden cross signals (50-day crossing above rising 200-day MA) yesterday, suggesting potential sector rotation broadening out from tech.

bullets.title: ETF inflows top $1T YTD; AAII stock allocations at 71%, well above 61.5% historical average
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reports ETF ecosystem volumes at 'full throttle' with YTD inflows exceeding $1 trillion. AAII survey shows June stock and stock fund allocations at 71%, significantly above the 61.5% historical average—a crowding signal for equity positioning.

bullets.title: UK designates MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL as critical third parties under direct financial regulatory oversight
bullets.body: The UK government designated Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Oracle as critical third parties to the UK financial sector, bringing them under direct regulatory oversight to protect financial system stability. Separately, Meta faces a potential €12B EU fine over addictive Instagram and Facebook feed design under the DSA.

bullets.title: NFLX engagement declining; JPM overweight but investor room skewed bearish pre-Q2
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag Netflix engagement (watch time, completion rates) declining despite healthy subscriber retention heading into July 16 Q2 report. Citi notes investor room skewed heavily bearish on multiple compression risk vs. traditional media (8–13x PE); NFLX needs stabilizing engagement, new product narrative, or large buyback to shift sentiment. JPMorgan maintains overweight at $118 PT expecting results largely inline with guidance.

bullets.title: PJM power prices rallied on hot weather/load growth; upside risk to TLN, CEG, VST estimates
bullets.body: PJM power spark spreads rallied this week alongside hot weather and load growth, driving higher scarcity pricing and re-rated risk premium across the curve. Morgan Stanley flags upside risk to utility earnings estimates; 2028/2029 capacity auction results due Tuesday post-close. TLN showed modest outperformance; CEG and VST also positioned to benefit.

bullets.title: Delta Q2 EPS $1.56 beats $1.48 est; guides Q3 revenue growth mid-teens—travel demand signal
bullets.body: Delta reported Q2 adjusted EPS $1.56 vs. $1.48 estimate on $17.67B revenue vs. $17.53B estimate, affirmed FY26 EPS guidance of $6.50–$7.50 and $3–4B free cash flow. Q3 EPS guided $2.00–$2.50 vs. $2.02 consensus; CEO says Delta will recover added fuel costs in Q3 via pricing power. Shares up 3% premarket—a positive read for consumer travel demand.

bullets.title: China helium export ban poses risk to semiconductor supply chains
bullets.body: China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports; helium is critical for semiconductor manufacturing and cooling of electronics equipment. This could create near-term supply chain friction for chip fabrication dependent on the commodity.
